authors: The majority of soft tissue tumours morphologically resemble mesenchymal tissues such as fat or smooth muscle
or consist of spindle cells or small round cells. A number of soft tissue tumours consist partly or wholly of epithelioid cells. These tumours
can provide a diagnostic challenge because of unfamiliarity with their morphology or their tendency to mimic epithelial
melanocytic or neuroendocrine tumours. Some soft tissue tumours are characteristically epithelioid
such as biphasic synovial sarcoma and others are usually non-epithelioid but can show an epithelioid growth pattern
such as epithelioid angiosarcoma. This case-based presentation will cover the more common types of epithelioid soft tissue tumours
describing an approach to diagnosis using morphology
